tagline.text: A minor basilica in Ilocos housing the Black Nazarene "Apo Lakay"

location.label: Location
location.text: Town center of Sinait, Ilocos Sur (about 36 km north of Vigan)

children.text: Sinait Church is the Minor Basilica of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino in the town of Sinait, Ilocos Sur, and a shrine to a dark-skinned image of Christ about 400 years old, known as "Apo Lakay." It was elevated to a minor basilica in February 2022, and pilgrims come especially on Fridays.

The official name of Sinait Church is the Minor Basilica of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino (Basilica Menor de San Nicolás de Tolentino), and it is also the Archdiocesan Shrine of El Santo Cristo Milagroso. It stands in the town of Sinait, Ilocos Sur, under the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia. According to Wikipedia, the church was founded in 1574 and completed in 1598, making it one of the oldest religious buildings in the Philippines. However, the Wikipedia article on the town of Sinait says the present church was built over eight years starting in 1660, so sources disagree on when it was built. This guide mentions both accounts and does not settle on an exact date. The church was first run by the Augustinians, passed to the secular clergy in 1772 and returned to the Augustinians in 1854. As for the town's name, one explanation says it comes from a local word meaning "contest" and that a letter was dropped in 1575 to give "Sinait," and the present name was officially adopted in 1913. The town had about 26,000 people (26,059) in the 2024 census.

The church is famous for the image on its altar, El Santo Cristo Milagroso (the Miraculous Holy Christ). It is a life-sized crucifix of about 400 years, and because its skin is dark it is also called the Black Nazarene; locals call it "Apo Lakay" (Grandfather). According to legend the image came from Nagasaki, Japan. Japanese Christians hiding from the persecution of the Tokugawa shogunate are said to have sent it floating out to sea in a wooden box together with a Marian image, La Virgen Milagrosa. It is said to be one of three religious statues that survived when the churches of Nagasaki were destroyed in 1614.

According to local accounts, a floating box was found in 1620 on the beach at the boundary between the village of Dadalaquiten Norte in Sinait and the village of Paguetpet in Badoc. The image of Christ was enshrined in Sinait, and the Marian image went to neighboring Badoc. A small chapel on the shore where the box landed still holds a small replica, it is said. Devotees believe the image heals the sick, and pilgrims come especially on Fridays, which earned Sinait the nickname "Quiapo of the North." Quiapo is the district of Manila with the Black Nazarene church.
The parish became an archdiocesan shrine and formally assumed minor basilica status on 16 February 2022. Find it in the
Philippine bishops’ shrine directory
under San Nicolas de Tolentino and Santo Cristo Milagroso de Sinait. Check the parish calendar for pilgrimage Masses and viewing of the image.

A life-sized dark-skinned image of Christ is enshrined in the lower center of the altar. It is about 400 years old, and pilgrimages continue because of the belief that it heals the sick. There may be lines of worshippers, so wait your turn and pay respects quietly.

The story goes that Japanese Christians fleeing persecution sent the image floating out to sea in a box together with a Marian image. It is also said to be one of three statues that survived when Nagasaki's churches were destroyed in 1614. Because it is a legend, it is better to take it as "said to be" than as established fact.

The church became an archdiocesan shrine in 2018, its elevation to a minor basilica was announced in 2021, and the official elevation Mass was held on February 16, 2022. It is the 19th minor basilica in the Philippines and the first in the Archdiocese of Nueva Segovia.

The architecture is described as Baroque. Look slowly at the façade and the altar decoration (retablo), and compare it with other old churches of Ilocos, a region prone to earthquakes. During Mass, it is polite not to go deep inside.

On the shore of Dadalaquiten Norte, where the box is said to have landed, there is a small chapel holding a small replica of the image. It is easier to go there by vehicle than on foot after visiting the church.

This nickname comes from the crowds of worshippers who gather on Fridays. If you want to see the church quietly, go early on a weekday morning; on Fridays you can feel the pilgrim atmosphere but it is crowded.
The Marian image from the same box is enshrined in the Saint John the Baptist Basilica in neighboring Badoc. Combining Sinait and Badoc on the same day lets you follow the legend in one trip.

Sinait is described as having the white-sand beach Cabangtalan (Imelda's Cove), the summer resort Lugo Beach and the Libunao Protected Landscape. You can add a seaside-town atmosphere to the church visit in one day trip. Travel time is needed between these places, so decide your priorities.
Have breakfast in Vigan and head to Sinait, which is described as about 36 km away.
Look around the exterior of Sinait Church and the square in front.
Go inside and spend a quiet time at the altar in front of Apo Lakay. During Mass, move so as not to disturb worshippers.
Have lunch in town and ask whether any shops sell local specialties such as garlic.
Go by vehicle toward the shore chapel at Dadalaquiten or Cabangtalan Beach and enjoy the sea view.
Return to Vigan around sunset.
The church itself needs only
1–2 hours
. Most of the day is travel time.
Pay respects to the Black Nazarene at Sinait Church.
Have a simple meal in town.
Go to neighboring Badoc and visit the Saint John the Baptist Basilica, where the Marian image is enshrined.
Move on to Laoag or Vigan and stay overnight.
Check locally how to get to Badoc and how long it takes.

If staying in Vigan first, look for a Sinait-bound jeepney in the Bantay–Vigan area. Before boarding, ask for the closest stop to the church in Sinait town proper.
Sinait’s municipality quotes about 35 km and
45 minutes
by road from Vigan. Allow extra time for jeepney stops and waits.

As of September 2023, Vigan's own airport reportedly had no scheduled flights. The nearest airport is Laoag International Airport (LAO), and flights between Manila and Laoag are reported to operate daily.
Confirm locally how to get from Laoag to Sinait and how long it takes.

The church is in the town center, so you can walk around town.
To the shore chapel or the beach, a car or tricycle is more convenient.
Northern Ilocos has a dry season from November to April and a wet season from May to October. The average temperature around Vigan is about
. The church is mostly indoors and can be visited in the rain, but the dry season is better if you want to reach the shore chapel or the beach.

The Garlic Festival is held in Sinait in early May. May 3 is also described as the feast commemorating the finding of the image, so a visit around this time is crowded and lodging fills up early. September 10 is the feast of Saint Nicholas of Tolentino. Dates and events may vary from year to year.

It is convenient to stay in Vigan's old town and visit Sinait as a day trip. Wikivoyage lists Vigan Hotel at about ₱500 for a double, Casa Teofila Lodge at about ₱1,079–1,476, Villa Angela Heritage House at about ₱1,500–2,800 and El Juliana Hotel at about ₱1,500. Prices change with the season, so check when you book.

Sinait is known for its Garlic Festival in early May, so you may find local garlic products. Typical dishes include Vigan empanada, sinanglao, arroz caldo, miki and okoy, and Wikivoyage lists Insiang's Empanada (
) and First Sinanglaoan (
). Both of these are in Vigan.
The church is a place of worship. Enter with shoulders and knees covered.
Fridays are busy with pilgrims. If you want a quiet visit, a weekday morning is better.
Refrain from photography and loud talk during Mass.
Queue and wait your turn to pay respects to the Black Nazarene, and follow the on-site instructions about touching.
In early May the Garlic Festival and pilgrimages overlap and it gets crowded, so book lodging early.
Plan transport from Vigan on a same-day round-trip basis in advance.
Bring a hat and water for the midday heat, and take breaks inside the church.
Look at the exterior from the square in front first, and go in when there is no Mass for a calmer visit.
The area around the church gets very crowded during events. Watch out for pickpockets and lost phones, and carry valuables in front of you.
The date of construction and the legend of the image differ among sources, so take the explanations in this guide as "said to be."
Mass times and opening hours may change, so check before you go.
Public transport timetables from Vigan to Sinait may change, so check locally.
During typhoon season (August–October), travel may be blocked or plans may change.
At the shore chapel and the beach, watch for waves and rip currents and follow safety signs.
The UNESCO World Heritage city of
Vigan
lies about
36km
to the south. It pairs well with Calle Crisologo, the cathedral and the museums.
The Saint John the Baptist Basilica in neighboring Badoc enshrines the Marian image of the same legend. Seeing it after Sinait completes the story.
Laoag
, the main city of Ilocos Norte, lies to the north and is close to an airport. Confirm travel time locally.
The UNESCO World Heritage
Paoay Church
is in Ilocos Norte. If you combine it into a one-day plan, leave plenty of time.
